skills.name: Right prisms: shape, faces, bases, vertices

note.text:
A prism is a solid with two identical, parallel faces called the bases, joined by rectangular faces called the lateral faces. In a right prism the lateral faces are perpendicular to the bases.
A prism is named after the shape of its base: triangular prism, rectangular prism (cuboid), pentagonal prism, hexagonal prism. A cube is a rectangular prism with all faces square.
Vocabulary: a face is a flat surface; an edge is where two faces meet; a vertex (plural vertices) is a corner where edges meet. The height of the prism is the distance between the two bases.
Examples: a Toblerone-style box (triangular prism), a matchbox or brick (cuboid), a pencil (hexagonal prism).

sections.heading: What is a prism?
sections.text:
Look at a brick, a matchbox or an unsharpened pencil. Each one has two ends that are exactly the same shape and size, and the ends face each other like the two covers of a book. These two ends are called the bases of the prism.
The faces that join one base to the other are called the lateral faces (lateral means 'at the side'). In a right prism they stand straight up from the base, at right angles, so each lateral face is a rectangle.

sections.heading: How a prism gets its name
sections.text:
A prism is named after the shape of its base, not after its sides.
• Base a triangle → triangular prism.
• Base a rectangle → rectangular prism (a cuboid). A cube is a cuboid whose faces are all squares.
• Base a pentagon → pentagonal prism. Base a hexagon → hexagonal prism, like a pencil.
To name a prism, find the two identical ends first, then count the sides of one of them.

sections.heading: Faces, edges and vertices
sections.text:
Every lateral face matches one side of the base. A hexagonal base has {n} sides, so a hexagonal prism has {n} lateral faces. Add the two bases: {n} + {2} = {prismFaces(n)} faces in all.
It has {n} edges round each base and {n} edges joining the bases: {prismEdges(n)} edges.
It has {n} corners on each base: {prismVertices(n)} vertices.

key_words.meaning: one of the two identical, parallel end faces
a side face joining the two bases (a rectangle in a right prism)
a flat surface of the solid
a line where two faces meet
the distance between the two bases

examples: A Toblerone box is a triangular prism: its two ends are triangles.
A brick and a matchbox are rectangular prisms (cuboids).
A pencil is a hexagonal prism: its ends have six sides.

mistake.wrong: A box with rectangular sides and triangle ends is a rectangular prism.
mistake.why: Name the prism after its two identical ends (the bases), not after its rectangular side faces: every right prism has rectangular sides.

worked_example.problem: The solid in the figure has two identical triangular ends joined by rectangles. Name it and its bases.
steps: The two identical, parallel faces are the bases: they are triangles.
A prism is named after its base: a {baseName(n, 'prism')} prism.
worked_example.answer: A {baseName(n, 'prism')} prism; its bases are the two triangles.
